prompt_title: Need a different way to take part? (optional)
prompt_body: During the sort, point, say, sign or show the adult an idea, a question or a change that would help you take part. You may pass or speak privately. The adult listens, says what can change and checks whether it helped.
policy_line: Codes from the Feedback & Marking Policy 2025/2026 (Pilot), Issue 1, May 2026, verified in session 2026-09-15 (SHA-256 41046284a00c9218679b946134cbc6e53c1897aad28b15fc4bd4aa963720ff3b).
codes: Evidence captured on the school's digital evidence platform
summary_line: Curriculum Policy 2026/27 §14.3 summary: VF WS I NS E R (six codes; NS “next step”, E “evidence on digital software app”, R “responded to feedback”). The Feedback Policy, the code source, adds // and ? and expands NS to one specific thing and R to loop closed.
launch_line: Lead with VF in the practical, sort and exit tasks. Written feedback is for extended writing only, strategic and not every piece (Curriculum Policy 2026/27 §14.3): here that means the Stretch explanation in the independent task, when it is worth a written next step.
staff_sections: Use regulation time, a trusted adult, accessible response routes and permission to refuse. The one small help prompt in We Do 2 is optional to open; genuine feedback is not optional and is not limited to that moment. Space: lung and breathing content can land close to home, so a pupil may work from the diagram and skip discussion.

The pupil responds in their own way: an edit in the margin in the same colour on the same page, a re-attempt, a verbal reply, a demonstration, a signed or symbol-chosen answer, or a captured comment. Voice is invited during the sort and again in the exit; it can be recorded as VF only when verbal feedback was actually given.

An adult genuinely reads, hears or watches the response and names what they heard back to the pupil. Add R only when the pupil responded AND the adult engaged with the response; no button, saved answer or completed exit supplies R on its own.

Change the next explanation, question, scaffold or task from what the pupil showed. In this lesson the sort tells you which example to re-model before the independent task; the exit tells you which route to open next lesson.

The particle diagram and the sort cards are models. The alveolus figures are supplied illustrations. Neither is a measurement; do not record either as practical evidence. The breath test comes in the next lesson and is the pupil's own observation.

Diffusion is examined in Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 Paper 1 Topic 1 and in Combined Science 1SC0. The same ideas run through Level 3 science and health routes, from nursing and paramedic practice, where gas exchange is the daily reality, to laboratory work on membranes and drug delivery.

A short explainer clip exists online; it is linked for staff only, never embedded, never autoplayed and never assumed available. The lesson does not depend on it. If used, play it with captions from the classroom screen.
Verbal, written, drawn, signed, symbol or choice selected, demonstrated or re-attempted, adult scribed. All count in the arrival, the sort and the exit.
